subject: history
title: MAIN Causes of World War I
welcome_lead: From the Balkans to the trenches, examine why Europe blundered into industrialised slaughter in 1914.
meta_desc: History Causes & Effects of Wars Adventure 1: long-term and short-term causes of the First World War.
final_note: You have surveyed the powder keg of pre-1914 Europe. Causation in history is always multi-layered.

walkthroughs.body_html: Historians often summarise the long-term causes with the acronym MAIN: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism and Nationalism. The Anglo-German naval race (HMS Dreadnought, 1906), competing colonial empires, the Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) opposing the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and ethno-nationalist tensions in the Balkans all contributed to fragility.

The Moroccan crises of 1905 and 1911, the Bosnian Annexation Crisis of 1908 and the Balkan Wars of 1912-13 entrenched rivalries. The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914 by Gavrilo Princip triggered the July Crisis. Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia, Russian mobilisation and German implementation of the Schlieffen Plan rapidly internationalised the conflict.

Interpretations range from Fritz Fischer's claim that Germany deliberately willed war to Christopher Clark's Sleepwalkers, emphasising shared responsibility and miscalculation. candidates should weigh structural and contingent factors and consider how decisions in Berlin, Vienna, St Petersburg, Paris and London each contributed.

options: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism
Military, Anarchy, Industry, Navy
Money, Arms, Ideology, News
Mobilisation, Assassination, Invasion, Negotiation

mcqs.q: Whose assassination at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914 triggered the July Crisis?
options: Archduke Franz Ferdinand
Kaiser Wilhelm II
Tsar Nicholas II
King Peter of Serbia

mcqs.q: Why was the monarchy restored in 1660?
options: Parliament voted to restore the monarchy because Cromwell had taxed them too heavily.
Charles II invaded England with a French army and seized the throne.
After Cromwell's death the Protectorate collapsed; General Monck negotiated Charles II's return on the terms of the Declaration of Breda (amnesty, religious flexibility, army pay).
Britain restricted immigration because the Commonwealth ceased to exist in 1962.

mcqs.q: Why did Britain restrict Commonwealth immigration from 1962?
options: Britain restricted immigration because the Commonwealth ceased to exist in 1962.
Britain restricted Commonwealth immigration because there was no work available.
Rising public hostility, political pressure, and economic concerns led to the 1962 Commonwealth Immigrants Act introducing voucher controls, followed by tighter restrictions in 1968 and 1971.
Parliament voted to restore the monarchy because Cromwell had taxed them too heavily.

mcqs.q: Why did the Soviet Union collapse in 1991?
options: A combination of economic stagnation, nationalist movements in republics, the failed August 1991 coup, and Gorbachev's reforms accelerating loss of control to Yeltsin.
The USSR collapsed because NATO invaded Moscow.
The USSR collapsed because Reagan outspent it in the arms race.
Britain restricted immigration because the Commonwealth ceased to exist in 1962.
